items.title: 23.2.1 Structure and Reactivity of the Carbonyl Group

source_refs.note: Topic 23.2.1 with Quick Check 23.1, printed pages 100-101 (PDF 103-104).

blocks.text: In carbonyl group >C=O, both carbon and oxygen are sp² hybridized. Carbon is bonded to an oxygen atom through a double bond and to other two groups through single bonds.

Carbonyl group is polar in nature because oxygen, being more electronegative, gets partial negative charge (δ⁻) and carbon gets partial positive charge (δ⁺). Two structural features of the carbonyl group determine the chemistry and properties of aldehydes and ketones.

items: The carbonyl carbon is electrophilic in nature due to its δ⁺ charge, and can be attacked by nucleophiles.

The double bond can undergo addition reactions because π bond is easily broken down. Moreover, planar shape of the group makes the carbonyl carbon uncrowded thus giving further support to addition reactions.

blocks.text: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones for two reasons. First; in a ketone, the electron releasing (inductive) effect of two alkyl groups reduces the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon making it less easily attacked by nucleophiles. Secondly, the two alkyl groups of a ketone tend to get in the way of attacking nucleophiles. This is also called steric hindrance.

blocks.alt: Methanal H2C=O, an aldehyde RHC=O and a ketone R2C=O in a row. An arrow above points left, labelled 'Increasing reactivity towards nucleophiles'; an arrow below points right, labelled 'Increasing steric hindrance'.

blocks.title: Quick Check 23.1
blocks.text:
a) Draw the structures for the following according to IUPAC system.
i) 2-,methylbutanal
ii) pentan-3-one
iii) 3-methylbutenal
d) 4- methylpentan-3-one
b) Name the following compounds (IUPAC) system).
i) C₆H₅–CHO
ii) (CH₃)₃C-CHO
iii) (CH₃CH₂CH₂)₂C=O
c) Rank the following compounds in order of increasing reactivity towards nucleophilic attack.
i) (CH₃)₃CCOCH₃
ii) (CH₃)₃CCOC(CH₃)₃
iii) (CH₃)₂CO

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The name 4-methylpentan-3-one breaks the IUPAC rule of lowest numbers: the chain is numbered from the end nearer the C=O and the branch, so the compound (CH₃)₂CHCOCH₂CH₃ is 2-methylpentan-3-one.
